title: Police cleared in prisoner's death
article: Provincial police officers have been cleared of any wrongdoing related to the death of a Harrowsmith woman who died after a drug bust.
Susan Maleska, 44, died in a police holding cell at the South Frontenac OPP detachment in the early morning hours of Feb. 24.

"The [autopsy] disclosed no anatomical cause of death and the toxicology exams revealed potentially lethal levels of an illegal substance," Rose Bliss, spokeswoman for the province's Special Investigations Unit, said recently.
The unit's director, James Cornish, has concluded that no OPP officers are criminally responsible for Maleska's death.

"The officers involved were dealing with a woman who had ingested a lethal quantity of a drug which had not yet begun to show its effects," Cornish said in a release. "By the time it did, the officers and [emergency services] personnel had insufficient time to act to save her life."
Maleska and her common-law husband, Bill Day, 49, were arrested for possession for the purpose of trafficking during a police drug search of their Harrowsmith Road home.

Around 2:50 a.m., 20 minutes after OPP officers had logged the couple into cells at the Frontenac detachment in the village of Hartington, Maleska went into medical distress. She was rushed to Kingston General Hospital where she was pronounced dead.
The provincial Special Investigations Unit, the civilian agency that investigates deaths and serious injuries involving police officers, picked up the case the same day.
Maleska was arrested on possession-related charges. When asked by officers if she had ingested any drugs before being arrested, she denied using any illicit drugs.
She was lodged into a police cell about 2:30 a.m. During their contact with Maleska, several officers said she appeared lucid and didn't appear to be under the influence of drugs.
An officer went to her cell around 2:50 a.m. and found she was unresponsive and convulsing.
An ambulance was called and attempts were made to put Maleska into the recovery position, the release said. Paramedics arrived at 3:14 a.m. to find Maleska with no vital signs.

They began and continued to try to resuscitate her at the detachment. On the way to the hospital, paramedics were able to establish a faint pulse at one point, but Maleska died at Kingston General Hospital.
Bliss wouldn't say what illegal substance was found in Maleska's blood, because that information may become evidence at another proceeding, such as a coroner's inquest.
